title: Private/VPC: Offline orchestration, artifact fallback, and upgrade contract
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Purpose: Define non-functional requirements, operational constraints, and concrete acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments operating with limited or no outbound egress (air-gapped or tightly filtered). This PRD focuses on artifact distribution, deterministic bootstrap, operator-safe upgrade sequencing, and fallback paths for cases where networked mirrors fail. We prioritize predictable upgrade safety for regulated customers while minimizing burst egress needs and providing an auditable manual fallback path.
background: Several enterprise pilots require upgrades and patching in closed networks or via scheduled minimal egress windows. Current acceptance artifacts overlap with prior canary and mirror docs but customers reported ambiguity in: (1) what constitutes a valid offline artifact set, (2) the exact operator behaviors during partial mirror failures, and (3) quantitative rollback thresholds. This ticket codifies those expectations into an operational contract and acceptance tests.
goals: Provide a deterministic offline bootstrap and staged upgrade flow that requires <=1 outbound egress window per major upgrade when mirrors are healthy
Define a signed artifact manifest format and attestable checksum protocol for customer verification
Specify operator safe-mode behavior, automatic rollback triggers, and manual intervention steps for air-gapped environments
Define fallbacks including physical-media and bastion-assisted staging when network mirrors are unavailable
out_of_scope: Continuous integration of model weights; runtime kernel tuning; Dedicated customer billing changes (covered by separate PRD)
requirements: Artifact packaging: release images + tarball manifest with canonical SHA256 checksums and PGP-like signature, documented format and minimal fields
Manifest validation: operator must validate manifest signatures before any node-level image activation
Mirror topology: support primary mirror, regional mirrors, and local airgap mirror (operator-managed file store)
Upgrade orchestration: staged per-control-plane quorum (operator) with configurable pause points and percent-based rollout (default 10% canary then 30% then 100%)
Rollback criteria (automated): service error rate increase >15% sustained for 10 minutes OR median p95 latency degradation >2x baseline OR failed health-check propagation to >20% of nodes
Operator safe mode: when mirror download fails, operator must enter a read-only safe mode that preserves ongoing inference traffic and queues upgrade operations for manual approval
Egress minimization: support differential delta images and sparse sync to limit bandwidth during network windows
Auditability: every offline sync, signature verification, and operator decision must be recorded in an immutable event log accessible via the customer control plane
Manual fallback: documented physical media procedure (USB/shipper) including manifest signing, receipt attestation, and deterministic import steps
Canary verification: synthetic workload harness that runs a defined prompt set and checks generation stability and latency to detect subtle regressions
Operator dry-run: ability to simulate an upgrade end-to-end without applying images, verifying download, signature, and rollout sequencing
acceptance_criteria: Given a private cluster with no outgoing HTTP allowed except to mirrors, an upgrade using the signed manifest completes successfully within a single scheduled mirror window when mirrors are healthy
When a mirror returns corrupted chunks, the operator rejects the image and does not proceed with node activation; event log includes checksum mismatch and affected nodes
Automated rollback triggers if synthetic harness regresion conditions (error-rate or latency) are met during canary phase; system returns to pre-upgrade image without manual steps in <=10 minutes
Operator safe-mode engages on partial mirror failures: control plane remains writable for traffic ops but blocks planned upgrades until manual approval
Physical-media import test: team performs full end-to-end import using shipped artifact and signed manifest; verification and audit events recorded and able to reproduce image checksum
Manifest signature verification is required and tested for all images: unsigned or tampered manifests are rejected in both online and offline import flows
Staged rollout policy honors percent thresholds; a 10% canary receives traffic and reports telemetry to the customer console to validate before proceeding
Bandwidth-limited sync: delta transfer reduces bytes transferred by >=60% compared to full image for typical patch updates in internal performance tests
All upgrade-related operator decisions surface a human-readable rationale and link to the event log in the control plane UI
test_plan: Simulated mirror outage: trigger partial mirror failures and assert operator enters safe-mode and blocks rollout
Checksum tamper: modify a single chunk on mirror and ensure operator detects and rejects artifact
Canary regression injection: deploy image with injected latency to canary nodes and verify auto-rollback behavior
Physical media rehearsal: QA team follows the physical-media import playbook and validates manifest signatures and checksums
Dry-run verification: run 'operator upgrade --dry-run' and assert all steps (download plan, verification, sequence) succeed without node changes
Telemetry and audit reproducibility: replay event log to demonstrate exact sequence and decisions over a 24-hour upgrade window
metrics_and_success: Mean time to safe upgrade completion during network window <= 4 hours for 3-region mirrors
Automated rollback success rate >= 95% when rollback criteria are met
Number of manual physical-media imports per quarter <= 2 for customers with configured mirrors
Bandwidth savings from delta syncs >= 60% on average for minor patches
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: signed manifest key compromise. Mitigation: rotate signing keys quarterly, provide customer-facing key fingerprinting and offline verification tool
Risk: incomplete telemetry in air-gapped installs. Mitigation: buffered telemetry store with deterministic upload protocol and local retention policies
Risk: customer operator unfamiliar with offline import. Mitigation: scripted import CLI with guided prompts, runbook, and 24/7 SE-assisted onboarding for first import
Risk: large image sizes exceed scheduled mirror window. Mitigation: enforce delta packaging, pre-warm mirrors, and audit bandwidth requirements during onboarding
open_questions: Should the default rollback latency/error thresholds be configurable per-customer or locked to a conservative default?
What is the canonical signing mechanism we ship? PGP-like or COSE-based attestation?
Do we provide a Redwood-managed mirror appliance (virtual) as a paid add-on for customers who cannot run mirrors?
What SLA do we guarantee for physical-media-assisted imports (turnaround, validation support)?
implementation_notes: Engineering to provide operator flags: --offline-manifest-path, --dry-run, --force-import, and a hook for custom canary verification scripts. Runtime team to expose API endpoints for synthetic harness results. Security to publish key-rotation playbook. PM to coordinate joint dry-run with 2 pilot customers in Cycle 10.
notes: This PRD intentionally focuses on the operational contract and acceptance tests. UX console changes for surfacing safe-mode and import events will be a separate PM ticket (see dependencies). Coordinate with Support for runbook creation and with Legal for export-control on shipped media.
follow_up: After acceptance, schedule a joint tabletop with 2 pilot customers to validate the physical-media import and mirror recovery scenarios
